chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, from his father, from Habba al-Urani, who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) went out to Al-Hira and said, 'This will connect to this,' and gestured with his hand towards Kufa and Al-Hira, 'Until the cubit of land between them is sold for dinars. And a mosque will be built in Al-Hira with five hundred doors, in which the Caliph of the Qa'im (may Allah hasten his reappearance) will pray, because the mosque of Kufa will be too cramped for them. And twelve righteous Imams will pray in it.' I said, 'O Commander of the Faithful, will the mosque of Kufa accommodate this, which you describe?' He said, 'Four mosques will be built for it: the mosque of Kufa is the smallest of them, and this one, and two mosques on the sides of Kufa, on this side and that side,' and he gestured with his hand towards the people of Basra and the two Ghariyyin.
ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali (peace be upon him) say about the future expansion of mosques in Kufa and Al-Hira?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights Imam Ali’s (AS) foresight regarding the urban expansion of Kufa and the eschatological significance of Al-Hira as a major prayer hub for the Caliph of the Qa'im (AS). The Prophet’s clarification that four mosques would be built underscores the anticipated growth of the Shia community, with specific references to the populations of Basra and Ghariyyin, reflecting the geographical spread of the faithful. It serves as a key narrative linking the historical development of Kufa to the future reign of the Twelfth Imam.
